name: Flexing for Nougat
summary: In Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka trades nougat for a little show. During Hallow's End, you flex for a sweet meant to cheer Spoops, a bedridden child.

sections.title: Tricks for Treats
sections.body: Hallow's End fills Azeroth's capitals with pranks and sweet-gathering. In Orgrimmar's inn, Innkeeper Gryshka keeps holiday sweets for those who join the custom. Your travels may bring dragons and dark sorcery, but here the bargain is plain: perform a trick or leave without a treat.

sections.title: Muscle on Display
sections.body: Innkeeper Gryshka asks you to show Orcish strength before she gives you Orgrimmar Nougat for young Spoops. Whatever disguise or armor you wear, strike a muscular pose. Even the Horde's feared fighters can amuse the common folk for candy.

faq.q: Who is asking for the flex?
faq.answer: Innkeeper Gryshka, keeper of the main tavern in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength, asks you to perform a trick before handing over holiday sweets.

faq.q: Why do I need to flex for candy?
faq.answer: Hallow's End custom asks for a small trick in exchange for a treat. Gryshka teases you with a request to display sheer physical power before she gives you candy.

faq.q: What is the Orgrimmar Nougat used for?
faq.answer: The nougat is one of four sweets gathered across the Horde's capitals to cheer Spoops, a sick orphan boy who is bedridden and cannot trick-or-treat on his own.
Innkeeper Gryshka keeps the counter at the main inn in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. She serves weary travelers and locals there.

faq.q: Can any Horde member participate in this?
faq.answer: Yes. Any member of the Horde can visit Innkeeper Gryshka during Hallow's End, strike a pose, and claim the seasonal sweet.

faq.q: What holiday is this a part of?
faq.answer: It is part of Hallow's End, an autumn festival that marks the end of the harvest and defies mortality with costumes, pranks, and sweets.

angles.text: Even veteran Horde champions who face deadly warlords flex their biceps for tavernkeepers, gathering festive sweets for the children.
As an Orc, you face a holiday test of pride when Orgrimmar's innkeeper asks you to show your muscle.
As a Warrior, you may take pride in devastating feats on the front lines. Yet it can be amusing or humbling to pose like a stage performer for festive candy.
